description: An enumerator's output bound to a loop variable and removed in the loop's body is the carrier wipe spelled as a compound statement, and until 2026-09-17 no tier read the enumerator on the Bash tool (DEF-830): the shape binds a loop variable rather than piping into a verb, so the hard tier answered nothing and the soft tier answered with its variable-operand nudge -- one confirm-by-re-issue in front of the whole-tree wipe, where the carrier spelling of the same wipe drew the wall. Three heads: the pipe into a read loop (the row's head), the for loop over a command substitution in either spelling (the everyday agent idiom), and the read loop fed at its tail by a process substitution or a here-string of one. Now the loop head binds the variable to the enumerator's output, so the enumerator's roots are the remove verb's operands as they are behind xargs, through the same tiers: the wall from a catastrophic root, the zone check on a protected root, the roster pass and one nudge for the rest. The body's operand must expand a name the loop binds; a body that removes a fixed operand is the rm tier's own. Declared limits, pinned as allows in the test class: a stage between the enumerator and the loop, the pipe on the line after the enumerator, a loop fed from a file, a word list beside a command substitution (read by neither head: beside a catastrophic word it draws the nudge where its twin walls, and behind the carrier-fed body it draws nothing -- a known silent allow with its own row) and the PowerShell statement-form loop (asked at the hook; the remove cmdlet's wall already). A fourth head landed 2026-09-18 (DEF-837): the for loop over a bare word list, which has no enumerator -- its roots are the list's words, judged one per word by the rm tier's own rule, so `for f in *` meets the wall `rm -rf *` meets while a narrowed word or a non-recursive body keeps the verdict its direct twin draws; like its sibling heads it walls a recursing body forced or not (the direct `rm -r *` did not until DEF-842 read recursion alone, the same day); the carrier-fed body behind that head was a silent allow until then.
fix_commit: the loop carrier lane, 2026-09-17 (DEF-830); the word-list head, 2026-09-18 (DEF-837)
